issue: भीर: a vocative भीरु (timid one) addressed to Kaikeyī, or भीड़/संकट (in this crisis).
our reading: हे भीरु / Timid one (address).
alternatives: भीर = distress: 'at this hour of distress you cast off trust and love'.

issue: जागति मनहुँ मसानु: 'मसान जगाना' is a cremation-ground rite performed in silence; how far to spell it out.
our reading: as if silently performing the rite of waking the dead (मसान जगाना) in a cremation ground.
alternatives: plainly 'as if awake in a cremation ground' (silent and grim as a burning-ground at night).

review: Agree with the doubt and with the reading बलि = बलिहारी; recorded only so the owner sees the reviewer agrees. The English "Bless you, my son" is a fair rendering of the endearment.
Agree it is a doubt. Our English adds "called the weak" and "grows"; the Hindi is the plain reading. Owner to decide between "a woman once strong" and "a woman, called weak, is strong".

issue: अबला प्रबल: "the weak one (woman) when strong" or "the woman, though called weak, is strong"
our reading: प्रबल हो उठी अबला / a woman, called the weak, once she grows strong
alternatives: अबला कहलानेवाली स्त्री वास्तवमें प्रबल है (a woman, though called weak, is mighty)

issue: बलि: Kaikeyī's endearment (बलिहारी) vs. an oath/adjuration
our reading: मैं तुमपर बलिहारी जाऊँ / Bless you, my son
alternatives: an earnest entreaty: I beg you

review: Agree with the writer's reading (Sītā, as mother, knowing him as her child, blessed him); no change.
Agree: बर qualifies बानी (fair speech); 'fully' is not an attested sense of बर. Fix above only rewords the line.
Agree: रूख = tree (the wish-granting tree made a mere tree), the plain reading.

issue: जननि जानि सिसु: who knows whom — the ascetic knowing Sītā as mother, or Sītā knowing him as her child (or both).
our reading: Sītā, as a mother, blessed him knowing him as her child.
alternatives: He placed the dust on his head knowing her as mother, and she blessed him as a child.

issue: बर बानी: whether बर qualifies बानी (excellent speech) or stands apart (बर = fully).
our reading: body, mind and excellent speech grow slack.
alternatives: they become wholly limp in body, mind and speech.

issue: रूख कलपतरु: रूख as 'tree' (made the wish-granting tree a mere tree) or 'dry, harsh'.
our reading: made the wish-granting tree a mere tree.
alternatives: made the wish-granting tree dry/harsh.

review: Partly disagree: तोषे is the finite verb and परिपोषे (plural, after बचन) reads most naturally as qualifying the words, 'gentle words nourished with love'; the writer's 'nurtured their love' adds 'their'. Leave for the owner; if the alternative is chosen, Hindi line 1: तब श्रीरामजीने प्रेमसे भरे कोमल वचन कहकर सब वनवासियोंको संतुष्ट किया। / English: Then, speaking gentle words full of love, Śrī Rāma contented all the forest folk.

issue: कहि मृदु बचन प्रेम परिपोषे: whether the words are full of love or the love (of the foresters) is nourished.
our reading: Gentle words that nurtured their love.
alternatives: Gentle words steeped in love (प्रेमसे परिपुष्ट वचन).

issue: राम बिरोधी हृदय तें प्रगट कीन्ह बिधि मोहि: either the Creator brought me forth from a heart (Kaikeyī's) hostile to Rāma, or the Creator has shown me to be Rāma's enemy at heart.
our reading: The Creator made me come forth from a heart hostile to Śrī Rāma.
alternatives: The Creator has made me out to be (revealed me as) hostile to Rāma at heart.

issue: रघुबर केतू: केतू may be Ketu the baleful comet/planet, applied to Bharata (I, like Ketu, am the cause), or 'Raghubara, the banner (of the Raghus)'.
our reading: Like the baleful Ketu, I alone am the cause of all these calamities.
alternatives: Śrī Rāma, the banner of the Raghus, is in the forest; I alone am the cause.

issue: राम प्रिय तात तुम्ह: 'Rāma is dear to you' or 'you are dear to Rāma'.
our reading: In word, thought and deed Śrī Rāma has always been dear to you (वचन मन काय describe Bharata's own love).
alternatives: You have always been dear to Śrī Rāma in word, thought and deed (Gita Press Hindi).

issue: जब तैं कुमति कुमत जियँ ठयऊ: कुमति may be an address ('O evil-minded one') or 'with an evil mind'.
our reading: When your evil mind resolved on this evil scheme.
alternatives: O evil-minded woman, when you resolved this evil scheme.

review: Disagree with the writer's reading: देखि is an absolutive, so line 3 has no finite verb and its gods, siddhas, ascetics, yogis and sages are the subject of न समरथु कोउ in line 4 (fixes given). Keep the doubt for the owner with the readings swapped.

Disagree: the plain reading is राम गिरि = Śrī Rāma's mountain (Rāmagiri, Citrakūṭa), a list with बन and तापस थल; 'with Śrī Rāma' needs a संग the verse lacks (fixes given). Keep the doubt for the owner with our reading changed to this.

issue: Lines 3-4: whether the gods, siddhas etc. are those who could not cross the river of love on seeing Videha's state, or the onlookers of his state while line 4 is Tulasīdāsa's general remark.
our reading: They all saw Videha's state; Tulasīdāsa says no one is able to cross the river of love.
alternatives: Of the gods, siddhas, ascetics, yogis and sages who saw Videha's state, none was able to cross the river of love (Gita Press).

issue: अटनु राम गिरि बन: roaming with Rāma, or roaming on Rāma's mountain (Kāmadanātha) and forests.
our reading: roaming the hills and woods and the haunts of ascetics with Śrī Rāma
alternatives: roaming Śrī Rāma's mountain (Kāmadanātha), its forests and the ascetics' places (Gita Press)

review: Agree it is a doubt, but the meaning should carry one plain reading. MW/Apte sakṛt: 'once, at once, once for all'; no 'seldom'. Our reading: swans in the one Mānasa lake only (the writer's alternative). The 'seldom' reading should be listed as the alternative instead.
reviewer_fix: {"id": "ayodhya.281.do281", "issue": "मानस सकृत मराल: sense of सकृत.", "our reading": "सकृत 'once, only': swans are in the one Mānasa lake only.", "alternatives": "सकृत as 'once in a while': swans are met with only seldom, in the Mānasa lake."}

issue: मानस सकृत मराल: sense of सकृत.
our reading: सकृत "once, seldom": swans are met with only seldom, in the Mānasa lake alone.
alternatives: सकृत as "only one (place)": swans are in the one Mānasa lake only.

issue: असमंजस: Sanskrit असमञ्जस (MW, Apte) is 'unbecoming, improper'; Hindi usage is 'dilemma, awkward fix'.
our reading: a boon that leaves me in a quandary (उलझनमें डालता है).
alternatives: an improper, unfitting second boon (the Sanskrit sense).

issue: भामिनी in समुझि धौं जियँ भामिनी
our reading: lady (address to Kaikeyī), MW bhāminī 1: a beautiful woman
alternatives: MW bhāminī 2: an angry or passionate woman (often an endearment and not always separable from sense 1); addressed to Kaikeyī in her sulking-chamber the sense 'angry lady' fits well. Owner to choose between 'lady' and 'angry lady'

issue: पितु बनदेव मातु बनदेवी: बनदेव and बनदेवी carry no number mark; our Hindi and English take them as plural (the gods and goddesses of the forest).
our reading: Plural: the forest gods will be your father and the forest goddesses your mother.
alternatives: Singular: the god of the forest will be your father and the goddess of the forest your mother (वनदेवता पिता, वनदेवी माता).

issue: मिटे दोष दुख दारिद दावा: दावा (Skt दाव: forest fire, heat, distress) as the fire of poverty only, as a fire of all three, or as a fourth item (burning distress).
our reading: my faults and sorrows are gone, and the burning of poverty too
alternatives: the fire of my faults, sorrows and poverty is quenched; faults, sorrow, poverty and burning distress are all erased

issue: अबिगत: Apte gives a-vigata only as 'not gone off, retained, present' (MW vigata 'gone away, disappeared'); neither gives 'unknown'.
our reading: अविज्ञेय | unknowable (the Hindi bhakti sense of अविगत).
alternatives: 'never departing, ever present, imperishable' (the Sanskrit sense: अ-विगत).

issue: नीलकंठ among the birds: Monier-Williams and Apte give for nīlakaṇṭha the bird senses peacock (first), gallinule, wagtail, sparrow, not the Indian roller; Hindi usage and the commentaries take नीलकंठ पक्षी as the Indian roller (blue jay).
our reading: Blue jays (Indian roller), as in the word suggestion of batch-14.words.jsonl.
alternatives: Peacocks (MW's first bird sense; मोर is not otherwise named in the list).

issue: पितु सुरपुर बन रघुबर केतू: केतू may go with मैं (I, like Ketu the baleful planet, am the cause) or with रघुबर (Rāma, the banner / chief of the Raghus, is in the forest); MW gives केतु 'flag, banner' and 'chief, leader, eminent person', so the second reading is fully supported by the dictionaries.
our reading: Like the baleful Ketu, I alone am the cause of all these calamities.
alternatives: My father is in heaven, Śrī Rāma, banner (crown) of the Raghus, is in the forest; I alone am the cause of every calamity.

issue: जब तैं कुमति कुमत जियँ ठयऊ: तैं is 'you' (as in 161.cau4 पेड़ काटि तैं), the subject of ठयऊ; MW gives कुमति both f. 'vile sentiment, folly' and mfn. 'foolish', so कुमति may be an adjective or address to तैं ('you, evil-minded one') rather than 'with an evil mind'. The English 'your evil mind resolved' makes the mind the subject.
our reading: Hindi: when you, with an evil mind, resolved on this evil scheme; English: when your evil mind resolved on this evil scheme.
alternatives: When you, evil-minded woman, resolved this evil scheme in your heart (English could read: When you, evil-minded one, resolved on this evil scheme, ...).
